title: An iterator as an inner class
description:
Make your own collection usable in a `for-each` loop.

```
for (int n : new Countdown(5)) -> 5 4 3 2 1
evens of 1..10 -> 2 4 6 8 10
sorted by length: [fig, pear, apple]
```
hints: An inner class `private class Steps implements Iterator<Integer> { int next = from; ... }` can read `from` from the outer object (lesson 7.01).
The filtering iterator must look ahead to know whether `hasNext()` is true: keep the next matching value in a field.
requirements: `class Countdown implements Iterable<Integer>` whose `iterator()` returns an instance of a private inner class.
`filter(List<Integer>, IntPredicate)` returns an `Iterator<Integer>` written as an anonymous class.
Sort words with a `Comparator` written as an anonymous class, then the same with a lambda.
stretch: Make `Countdown` take a step and support counting down by 2s.
